name: Mexican Mint Marigold

facts.how: Fresh or dried as a tarragon substitute and tea
facts.where: Gardens and naturalized in Central/South Texas

caution: A well-known culinary herb; confirm the sweet anise scent. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Narrow glossy leaves that smell strongly of anise, topped by small golden marigold flowers in fall.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Texas cooks use it as 'Texas tarragon,' and its leaves make a sweet, licorice-like tea.
